PullRequest.Title: Agents - fix diff order in the Changes tab when toggling views
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request addresses an issue in the Agents window's "Changes" tab where the diff editor list was not updating correctly when switching between "View as List" and "View as Tree". 

### Changes made:
- Updated the `changesMultiDiffSourceResolver.ts` to:
  - Read the current view mode from the Changes view.
  - Sort diffs using the shared helper `sortMultiDiffEditorFileListItems`, ensuring consistency with the Changes view's sorting logic.
  - Removed the previous sorting function to avoid redundancy.
  
- Added a regression test in `changesMultiDiffSourceResolver.test.ts` to verify that the diff order updates correctly when toggling between view modes.

### Key points:
- The Changes tab now correctly reflects the order of files based on the selected view mode.
- The implementation ensures that previously loaded diffs are reused, maintaining their collapsed state without reloading.
- The existing tests were updated to include the new view mode, and all tests passed successfully. 

This fix enhances the user experience by ensuring that the displayed diffs are consistent with the user's selected view preference.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents Changes multi-diff editor with a session containing many changed files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The resolver reads the already-available active-session change array, sorts it in memory, allocates one MultiDiffEditorItem per change, and publishes the resources before the editor can build its document list. Text-model resolution then remains on the existing editor-model path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create original and modified text-model references for each diff resource; providers may read local, virtual, or remote content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold open: up to two model-reference resolutions per changed file, concurrently; warm cached resources reuse URI-keyed mapped entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resources entered the same model-reference creation path before the PR; only their source ordering algorithm differed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold model creation must finish before the document set is published; this boundary is downstream of the changed in-memory sort.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N active-session changed files. List mode remains O(N log N) path comparison as before; tree mode builds O(N) path-tree state plus sibling sorting. Effective cardinality is one resource per distinct change, with downstream model caching keyed by original/modified URI pairs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sorting and item construction are synchronous and single-threaded. On a cold open, the unchanged MultiDiffEditorInput starts original/modified model-reference creation with Promise.allSettled per item and Promise.all across items; the diff neither increases this concurrency nor adds a new boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold editor open, downstream mapObservableArrayCached has no entries and resolves text models for every resource, as it did before. Existing entries are keyed by URI pairs and survive pure reordering; no negative-cache behavior is changed by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk and helper establish only synchronous sorting/allocation, while the downstream URI-keyed mapper proves model references are cached independently of item identity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions can vary from a few files to large generated change sets, but the added tree grouping is only selected for tree mode and replaces the prior path sort rather than adding a boundary or an extra collection pass on a repeated hot event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The list path retains the prior asymptotic cost, and the tree path performs bounded in-memory work needed to produce the requested ordering without adding I/O or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the Changes view between list and tree while its multi-diff editor is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view-mode observable invalidates resourcesObs, which reorders N changes and publishes the reordered resource list; the editor then updates document order. This occurs once per explicit toggle and is on the immediate UI action path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential text-model provider reads behind createModelReference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero new model-reference resolutions for a pure view-mode reorder because URI-keyed cache entries are retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, toggling the Changes view did not republish source order. Existing models were already loaded; the PR changes only their published order and preserves those cached models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on the warm toggle critical path; only in-memory reorder and observable/UI update occur.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N changed files in the active session; each explicit toggle performs one O(N log N)-class reorder and O(N) item/result allocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No parallel or queued work is introduced by the changed sort. Observable propagation is synchronous; downstream model entries are reused rather than resolving concurrently again.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: New MultiDiffEditorItem wrappers have the same original/modified URI key. mapObservableArrayCached reuses the existing RefCounted document/model entries, so a warm toggle does not recreate text models or reload file contents.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: viewModeObs is the new dependency, and URI-pair cache keys in MultiDiffEditorInput preserve model references across wrapper replacement and reordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact rendering cost depends on the number of visible diffs and editor implementation, but the traced model path rules out file reloads and the action is user-triggered rather than frame-, scroll-, or input-frequency work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. One bounded in-memory sort per explicit mode toggle is necessary for the feature, and costly model/file work remains cached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive an active-session changes update while tree mode is selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An activeSessionChangesObs update invalidates changesObs/resourcesObs; the resolver builds the tree ordering and publishes a new resource list. Existing changes reuse downstream URI-keyed entries, while only genuinely added resources need model resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve text models for added or URI-changed diff resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two references per newly added/changed URI pair; unchanged resources perform no new boundary call due keyed caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same active-session update resolved only new URI keys and disposed removed keys; the PR substitutes tree ordering for flat path ordering when tree mode is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New resources wait for their model references before the updated document set publishes; the changed sort adds only preceding CPU work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N total changed files after the update and A newly added or URI-changed entries. Sorting scales with N; expensive model work scales with A, not N, after cache reuse.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changed tree construction is synchronous. Existing downstream model creation may resolve up to two sides for each of A added entries and allows aggregate concurrency across those additions, but that behavior and cardinality predate the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive entries for unchanged URI pairs are reused. Removed keys are disposed and newly introduced keys are resolved exactly as before; the diff does not alter failure/negative-cache semantics.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable dependencies and downstream key selection directly establish update frequency and effective expensive-work cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Change-update frequency and maximum session size vary, but no evidence shows a high-frequency source or a new boundary fan-out; the additional tree allocation is linear and short-lived.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The helper changes ordering work but does not defeat model caching, increase boundary cardinality, or introduce unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced the new view-mode dependency through sorting, observable publication, multi-diff document caching, and model-reference boundaries. The PR adds bounded in-memory reorder work on open, session updates, and explicit view toggles, while URI-keyed caches preserve loaded diffs and prevent reload fan-out; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
